title: Remarks at Athens, Tennessee
paragraphs: I wish to thank you for giving me this opportunity of saying a word of greeting to you. I am glad to stop here at the seat of the Grant University; a university from which so many men have gone into public life. It has been the most genuine pleasure to be here in your beautiful country of East Tennessee. I have been glad to see your growing cities. It is a mighty good thing to have manufactories and railroads. It is a better thing to have good men and good women. I am glad to see your universities. It is a great thing to have training, intelligence. There is something still more important and that is character/ it is a fine thing to have intellect; it is a finer thing to have character in private and in public, just as you have honesty between neighbor and neighbor.
